answer: Admission to this registry is a sonnet, not a signature: every applying identity must submit a fresh text standing at least a third of its lines away from every entry already filed. Each new entry widens the exclusion volume around the corpus, so the open mesa of admissible phrasing narrows as the roll grows and the cost of finding one more distinct piece climbs faster than the number of applicants. A thread ties each sonnet to the entries it was measured against, exposing copied templates, and a farm of a thousand aliases must clear the same rising bar a thousand times in a crowded space.
